Omit ordinary participant records, reply/forward headers, numeric sender IDs, personal ticket references, attachments and unrelated personal information. limitations: Raw export remains outside the repository; its hash is an integrity reference, not independent authentication or a certified capture time.

Live Telegram message retrieval was unavailable through the web tool during this review. Links are constructed from the public group handle and export message IDs; live existence/content not reverified.
Deleted/inaccessible messages and previous edits are not recovered. The observed range is not a completeness guarantee.
Fusion HTML export is present but not analyzed in this first Chainge-focused pass. Media and linked external announcements are not exhaustively reviewed.
Earlier reposted explanations are discovery leads only until original official sources and roles are verified. No ordinary-member messages are published.
This is a communications timeline. No issuer restriction, custody attribution, funding receipt or user repayment is independently established by an announcement.

638119.author: DJ Qian (@djqian)
638119.excerpt:
After identifying an OTP related vulnerability in the beginners' mode wallets, we have taken immediate action to ensure the safety of your assets. 

As a precautionary measure, certain Chainge features have been temporarily paused. 

We are diligently working to resolve the issues and aim to resume normal operations as soon as possible. 

Rest assured, the security of your assets remains our top priority and we are currently working on a recovery tool for all users in beginner mode to use and migrate to self-custodial expert mode.

Thank you for your patience and steadfast support.

897496.author: DJ Qian (@djqian)
897496.excerpt:
Hello everyone,

I know these last few months have brought a lot of uncertainty and frustration. Many of you have been waiting far too long for a resolution, and I want you to know I’ve taken that seriously. That’s why I made the decision months ago to use my own personal funds to help solve this.

It hasn’t been easy. Most of my money is currently locked in a crypto fund that doesn’t allow early withdrawals. To speed things up, I accepted penalties and gave up any future profit just to get access to the funds as soon as possible.

Today, I can finally share something clear and concrete:

The first part of the funds will be released on Friday, August 1st.

From that day, a total of $3.752M will start being distributed gradually over the next 28 days.

I will personally explain the full process for restoring everyone’s funds, step by step, once it starts.

This first step won’t solve everything at once, but it will officially begin the compensation process. More parts will follow after this. Every stuck transaction will be fully resolved — that promise stays.

Also: FsnScan is expected to be back online next week, as a full node sync is required.

Until now, I’ve been very hesitant with giving new timelines because of delays that were out of my control. But now, things are finally moving forward.

I have already signed an official release execution paper with the fund, confirming that the transfer of funds starts this Friday. My lawyer has been involved in every step and has also prepared backup solutions in case anything unexpected happens.

Also, I want to say clearly: I hear your frustration. I understand it.

I’m not going anywhere.
I will stay here with you until all transactions are cleared and everything is back on track.

At the end of this whole process, I will also hold a live AMA and answer all the remaining questions openly.

Thank you for your patience and trust.

— DJ

entries.title: Earlier, separate interruption: beginner-mode vulnerability
entries.summary: DJ reported an OTP-related vulnerability in beginner-mode wallets, a precautionary pause of some features and work on a recovery/migration tool.
entries.eventTime: Reported as ongoing on publication date.
entries.limitation: This establishes a reported interruption, not a connection to the later liquidity problem.

entries.title: wKAS bridge queue and bug workaround
entries.summary: DJ said the queue had cleared, but a bug still needed fixing; he described a route through USDT in the dapp to convert wKAS to native KAS.
entries.eventTime: Reported current status; exact bug onset unspecified.
entries.limitation: This is a claim about one route. It does not establish that all assets or withdrawals were functioning.

entries.title: Admin describes KAS bridge pause and planned vault migration
entries.summary: Tanvir described a system migration for a new KRC-20/KASPA platform, with the bridge expected to reopen by the end of January. In a later message that day, he said vault addresses would be updated and an asset-proof mechanism would follow the migration.
entries.eventTime: Statements published 16 January 2025; end-of-month reopening was an expectation, not a verified completion date.
entries.limitation: An admin communication about KAS routes. It does not establish when the pause began, identify the old or replacement vaults, prove reserve coverage, or show that the migration or asset-proof mechanism was delivered. It does not establish a link to the later blacklisting explanation.

entries.title: Backlog acknowledged; 14 March target
entries.summary: DJ acknowledged stuck transactions, said he had worked on them for about two weeks, and targeted 14 March for clearing the backlog. CUSDT/KAS activation and reopening the wKAS/KAS bridge were described as subsequent steps.
entries.eventTime: Target: 2025-03-14; reopening conditional on backlog clearance and wKAS repegging.
entries.limitation: Two weeks describes his claimed work period, not an independently established start date for all disruptions.

entries.title: Blacklisting explanation and personal-funding plan
entries.summary: DJ attributed depleted liquidity to fund-holding addresses being blacklisted after alleged illicit use of the service. He said lawyers had been working on the matter for about two months and that he would use personal funds while awaiting its resolution.
entries.eventTime: Retrospective claim of legal work for roughly two months; no precise restriction date.
entries.limitation: No specific issuer, chain-qualified address, restriction transaction or authority is identified in this message. Neither the restriction nor the alleged cause is independently established by this timeline.

entries.title: Funding expected within four days; 473 transactions remaining
entries.summary: DJ said he expected all his funds to arrive within at most four days and reported 473 stuck transactions remaining.
entries.eventTime: Funding target relative to 2025-03-14; backlog count as stated that day.
entries.limitation: The count and funding expectation are statements, not a reconciled claims ledger or proof of payment.

entries.title: Admin says initial BTC issues spread to other assets
entries.summary: Tanvir referred to an earlier published article about vault blacklisting and said BTC transactions were initially affected before the problem spread to other assets.
entries.eventTime: Retrospective statement published 14 March 2025; initial onset and expansion dates are unspecified.
entries.limitation: This records the admin’s explanation, not independent confirmation of a restriction. The referenced earlier article has not been identified and verified. No issuer, restricted address, chain, or specific additional asset is identified in this excerpt.

entries.title: One-fifth reportedly resolved; further funds awaited
entries.summary: DJ reported resolving one-fifth of the stuck transactions using money already available, while the larger funding amount was still awaited.
entries.eventTime: Reported progress as of publication; further funds expected that night or next day.
entries.limitation: No denominator or independent payout reconciliation is supplied in this statement. Do not combine this fraction with another date's count as an audited total.

entries.title: Earlier funding estimate acknowledged as missed
entries.summary: DJ said the money expected the prior week had not arrived and that he was still waiting for funds to settle the transactions.
entries.eventTime: Retrospective reference to the preceding week.
entries.limitation: This is an acknowledgement of an unmet estimate, not independent evidence of the fund or its terms.

entries.title: Separate AWS/domain interruption reported as recovered
entries.summary: DJ attributed a service interruption to AWS/domain problems, said backend systems continued running and that it would not affect resolving stuck transactions, then reported service recovery.
entries.eventTime: AWS explanation at 02:05 UTC; recovery claim at 04:38 UTC on 2025-03-26.
entries.limitation: Recovery here must not be read as confirmation that the withdrawal backlog was settled. The cause is attributed, not independently diagnosed.

entries.title: Two funding sources described; no firm ETA
entries.summary: DJ described two places from which he was seeking funds, one as a backup, and said he could not commit to an ETA despite expecting progress that week or the next.
entries.eventTime: Conditional expectation, not a confirmed payment date.
entries.limitation: No counterparties, receipts or independently verified funding commitments are established.

entries.title: Crypto-fund withdrawal constraints and conditional settlement plan
entries.summary: DJ said early withdrawal from a crypto fund required waiting for liquidity. He expected about 5 million USDT within three days once the withdrawal succeeded and anticipated resolving pending orders within a week after receiving funds.
entries.eventTime: Conditional milestones: successful withdrawal, receipt of funds, then settlement.
entries.limitation: The three-day period is conditional on withdrawal success, not an unconditional three days from the announcement. No independent confirmation of funding or settlement is provided.

entries.title: Updates tied to actual receipt of funds
entries.summary: DJ said he would update the group when he had received funds and subsequently said he had no update.
entries.limitation: These statements describe his update policy; they do not independently establish funding status.

entries.title: Service suspended pending liquidity injection
entries.summary: DJ explicitly stated that service was suspended until he injected liquidity.
entries.eventTime: Suspended as stated on publication date; no restoration date.
entries.limitation: The message gives no technical scope or exact start time of the suspension. It does not date the first affected withdrawal.

entries.title: Liquidity injection still described as pending
entries.summary: DJ said liquidity injection remained his priority but that he could not provide an exact ETA.
entries.eventTime: Current status as stated on publication date.
entries.limitation: A statement of intended action, not confirmation that liquidity had been supplied.

entries.title: 1 August start and 28-day distribution schedule announced
entries.summary: DJ announced that a first funding tranche would be released on 1 August and that $3.752 million would start being distributed over the next 28 days. He also said he had signed release-execution paperwork and expected FsnScan back online the following week.
entries.eventTime: Announced start: 2025-08-01; duration: 28 days; no timezone specified for the target date.
entries.limitation: The schedule, paperwork and explorer restoration are claims. Receipt, distribution and restoration require separate evidence.

entries.title: First tranche not yet received
entries.summary: DJ said the first tranche had been confirmed for Friday but had not yet reached him.
entries.eventTime: As of publication on 2025-08-02, following the 1 August target.
entries.limitation: A reported delay, not evidence that a transfer was sent or credited.

entries.title: First tranche described as a cheque
entries.summary: DJ said a cheque was in his agent's possession and that he had expected cryptocurrency such as USDT instead.
entries.eventTime: Reported on publication date; proposed further detail on Monday.
entries.limitation: Possession of a cheque is not a cleared balance or a payout to users.

entries.title: Cheque deposit reported
entries.summary: DJ said he had deposited the first cheque and was continuing to recover his funds.
entries.eventTime: Deposit reported retrospectively; exact deposit date unspecified.
entries.limitation: This does not establish clearance, amount, liquidity injection or user settlement.

entries.title: Small receipt reportedly used for debts and operations
entries.summary: DJ said legal efforts to unlock the blacklisted address continued and that a small amount received had been used to pay debts and keep operations running; he linked settlement to receiving more.
entries.eventTime: Retrospective small receipt; further settlement conditional on more funds.
entries.limitation: The amount and recipients are unspecified. This is not evidence that user claims were settled.

entries.title: Further progress expected in ten days
entries.summary: DJ said he appeared likely to receive good news within ten days. This is the latest message from the confirmed founder account in this retained Chainge export.
entries.eventTime: Forward-looking expectation from 2025-10-09; outcome unverified.
entries.limitation: No promised settlement date or confirmed outcome. No later retained messages from this account does not prove silence on other channels or absence of deleted messages.
